# nyc42.lol — what's on in New York City

> Listings and news for New York City. Every entry names the source it came from and the day it was checked against it. Independent publication: not a government outlet, not a ticket seller, not affiliated with any venue.

How this site works, in five rules:

- **Every fact names where it came from, and when we last looked.** The source prints as text, never as a live link.
- **Nothing is listed on a date we could not confirm.** If the organiser said "early November" and nothing more, no invented day appears here — the missing day appears instead.
- **What's on, not what went wrong.** No politics, no crime, no tragedy.
- **We pick the best, and say why.** Picking out the best of something is the job; running a named business down is not.
- **A page exists when there is something to put on it.** No empty templates waiting for content.

## What a reader finds here

- [Events](https://nyc42.lol/events/): events on dates confirmed with the organiser, with times, prices and running order where the organiser published them.
- [News](https://nyc42.lol/news/): what changed in the city. Long pieces carrying the whole calendar or the whole figure, not a wire paragraph.
- [About](https://nyc42.lol/about/): the rules above, written out at length.

## Where the facts come from

The organiser, or the publication that reported it: Time Out New York, Gothamist, The City, The New York Times, and the organisers themselves. Each entry prints that name and the date it was verified. Venue coordinates are geocoded once and stored in the data; where the geocoder returns the wrong place, the entry publishes without a map rather than with a wrong one.

Where a voice from Reddit appears in the text, it is a direct quotation from a public post, attributed to the subreddit rather than to the person.

What has not been announced is said to be unannounced. A closing date nobody has given, a theme not yet confirmed and a running order still to come are three things this site names rather than fills in.

## Events

- [Village Halloween Parade 2026](https://nyc42.lol/events/village-halloween-parade-2026/): The 53rd parade goes up Sixth Avenue at 7pm on Saturday 31 October. Watching is free, joining in is free if you are in costume, and it happens rain or shine.
- [Open House New York Weekend 2026](https://nyc42.lol/events/open-house-new-york-weekend-2026/): Three hundred buildings across the five boroughs open for one weekend, 16–18 October. The full lineup is revealed on 25 September and tickets go on 2 October.
- [New York Comic Con 2026](https://nyc42.lol/events/new-york-comic-con-2026/): Four days at the Javits Center, 8–11 October, for NYCC's twentieth anniversary — with a Coney Island theme and the panel schedule already published.
- [NYC Broadway Week: two-for-one at 25 shows](https://nyc42.lol/events/broadway-week-fall-2026/): Two weeks of 2-for-1 Broadway tickets across 25 productions, from 8 to 20 September 2026. Tickets have been on sale since 18 August.

## News

- [Broadway Week: which of the 25 is it for](https://nyc42.lol/news/broadway-week-which-shows-are-worth-it/): Twenty-five shows take the two-for-one from 8 to 20 September. They are not equally worth it, and the reason has less to do with the shows than with what each one costs the rest of the year.
- [The Brooklyn Museum sets out its autumn](https://nyc42.lol/news/brooklyn-museum-fall-2026/): Six new shows open in October: manga in the Great Hall, fifty European masterpieces from the Pearlman Collection, Hopi kachina dolls and an installation in the lobby about the Tuskegee Airmen.
- [Disney will sail from New York again in 2027](https://nyc42.lol/news/disney-cruises-return-to-nyc/): The Disney Wish returns to New York in autumn 2027 after four years away: seven sailings, five of them to Bermuda, one a foliage run to Boston, Saint John and Halifax. Booking opens 8 September.
- [Hudson foliage cruise tickets are on sale](https://nyc42.lol/news/hudson-river-foliage-cruises/): Circle Line has two foliage sailings this September: an eight-hour run to Bear Mountain on the 19th and 20th, and a four-hour trip toward Hook Mountain on the 26th and 27th. Last year sold out.
